method.reason: Use the B3LYP hybrid functional (20% HF exchange) for this closed-shell organic conformational scan; the ORCA manual entry documents B3LYP as a popular hybrid functional. No dispersion correction is claimed because the retrieved official excerpt does not document one.

sources.quote: The popular B3LYP functional (20% HF exchange) as defined in the TurboMole program system (LDAOPT C_VWN5)

basis.reason: Use the Karlsruhe def2-TZVP polarized valence triple-zeta orbital basis, available for H–Rn, as a balanced basis for carbon/hydrogen conformational energies.

sources.quote: For example, the Karlsruhe def2-TZVP basis set can be invoked via the def2-TZVP keyword.

proposal.reason: The Request permits automatic selection of method and basis. Completed current-Run knowledge.search Results provide official ORCA documentation for both selections. I choose B3LYP/def2-TZVP before geometry preparation or execution, as required.
